done_when: The owner switches a repo to agent merges with one command run in their own terminal

findings.body: The owner-only check applies only to `enable`. In an unsigned client prototype, `repo.merge_setting()` returns `agent` even while the default branch says `human` (src/forge/repo.py:174-177). A ready switch pull request can therefore pass through `forge merge let-the-agent-merge` and reach `gh pr merge` (src/forge/merge.py:68-73). `forge merge` needs to refuse pull requests that change the merge setting.
findings.title: Not done: The agent never makes the switch and points you to the command.

findings.body: Any existing `fix/let-the-agent-merge` branch causes an unconditional refusal. An interrupted run after worktree creation, commit, push, or pull-request creation cannot be resumed with `forge merge enable`; the owner is instead sent to a second command. The check also labels an unrelated branch as the switch without examining its recorded purpose or changes. Identify the command's own fix and continue it safely.
findings.title: Not done: You switch a repo to agent merges with one command.

findings.body: This call uses `forge close` without a switch-specific owner-merge rule. The earlier ruling relies on close's human-merge Ready line, but an unsigned client prototype follows its agent branch instead: src/forge/close.py:142-152 prints `Next: forge merge let-the-agent-merge`. That instruction would let the agent merge the permission change. The switch fix must always tell the owner to merge its pull request.
findings.title: Keep the switch fix's close output on the owner's merge path

findings.body: The added exception changes only the `started` status. In a prototype, a ready switch fix still gets `Next: forge merge <item>` from src/forge/nextstep.py:384-386, and the green-checks waiting state still says it is preparing an automatic merge at src/forge/nextstep.py:403-408. Those messages contradict the required owner-only path at stages after the fix starts.
findings.title: Keep forge next on the owner's merge path for the switch fix

findings.body: The required default-branch check is absent before `story.add_worktree()`. `repo.check_pin()` only validates the installed version (src/forge/repo.py:293-325), so invoking `forge merge enable` from another branch creates and closes the switch fix instead of refusing without changes.
findings.title: Refuse enable when the owner is outside the default branch

findings.body: `Path.read_text()` reads CRLF through universal-newline translation; writing the resulting string as UTF-8 bytes at line 158 changes the entire file to LF. A valid CRLF `forge.toml` therefore loses its line endings even though the switch is meant to preserve them. The table test uses LF only.
findings.title: Preserve the requested forge.toml line endings

findings.body: The rerun test explicitly accepts the refusal that breaks interrupted one-command recovery. The file has no command-level cases for interruption before commit, after push or pull-request creation, unrelated same-name fixes, prototype agent-merge refusal, or the switch fix's `forge next` output. Its skill check at line 75 reads committed source files rather than exercising `forge sync`, so it cannot detect a broken delivered skill.
findings.title: Not done: tests/test_merge_enable.py

findings.body: The new `merge-enable` kind creates a special state path and a separate `forge next` branch, although the fix's recorded `why` and `done_when` can identify it before the config edit. Using the existing fix kind removes that extra distinction while retaining collision checks.
findings.title: Simpler: merge-enable kind → existing fix kind and recorded purpose

why: Nothing in the flow can switch a repo to agent merges: Forge tells the owner to ask the agent, and the agent's own permission checks rightly refuse to loosen a gate on itself
